desc: Indian private bank, the third-largest in the country, offering retail, corporate and wealth banking, cards and Citi India's consumer business.
markets: Customers across India through thousands of branches, with limited overseas offices.
rationale: Large Indian bank with a strong marketing culture; F1 supports premium positioning, though customers are domestic.
changed: Acquired Citi India's consumer business in 2023

name: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena
desc: Italian bank founded in 1472, the world's oldest surviving bank, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, wealth and insurance.
markets: Customers in Italy; the state has been a shareholder since its 2017 rescue.
rationale: Italian bank with a domestic customer base; the Italian Grands Prix offer local hospitality but international value is limited.

name: BBVA
desc: Spanish bank with large operations in Mexico, Turkey, Spain and South America, serving retail, SME and corporate customers.
markets: Operates in Spain, Mexico, Turkey and South America, with corporate banking offices elsewhere.
rationale: Global bank in a category where Santander already sponsors F1; Spanish and Mexican Grands Prix fit its main markets.

name: Bank of Baroda
desc: Indian public sector bank founded in 1908, with thousands of branches in India and operations in 17 countries.
markets: Mainly India, with branches and subsidiaries overseas, including in the Gulf, Africa, the UK and Asia.
rationale: State-controlled retail bank serving the Indian diaspora abroad; modest marketing budget and limited F1 fit.

name: Bank of India
desc: Indian state-owned commercial bank founded in 1906 and nationalised in 1969, offering retail, corporate, SME and agricultural banking.
markets: Mostly India, with overseas branches in several countries including the UK, Singapore and the Gulf.
rationale: Government-owned bank with a modest marketing profile; F1 would offer limited return for its customer base.

name: Bank of Jiangsu
desc: Chinese joint-stock commercial bank based in Nanjing, offering corporate lending, retail banking and wealth management.
markets: Serves customers in Jiangsu province and other Chinese regions; no international operations known.
rationale: Regional Chinese bank with no overseas retail presence; limited reason to buy global F1 exposure.

name: Bank of Montreal
desc: One of Canada's five largest banks, founded in 1817, offering personal, commercial, wealth and capital markets banking as BMO.
markets: Serves Canada and the US, with its US banking business accounting for a large share.
rationale: North American bank; the Canadian and US Grands Prix offer hospitality for commercial clients across both markets.

name: Blue Owl
desc: New York alternative asset manager investing in private credit, real estate and GP stakes for institutional and private investors.
markets: Raises capital from investors and invests mainly in the US, with offices in Europe and elsewhere.
rationale: Asset manager courting institutional investors; F1 hospitality could support investor relations, but it has no consumer products.
changed: Formed in 2021 by SPAC merger of Owl Rock and Dyal Capital

name: Broadridge
desc: Fintech provider of investor communications, proxy voting, securities processing and wealth technology, spun off from ADP in 2007.
markets: Serves banks, brokers and asset managers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B fintech with global banking clients; F1 hospitality and technology showcase suit client entertainment.

name: Canara Bank
desc: Indian public sector bank founded in 1906 and nationalised in 1969, providing retail, corporate, agriculture and MSME banking.
markets: Customers across India through thousands of branches, with a small overseas presence.
rationale: State-owned bank serving domestic customers with a modest marketing budget; limited F1 relevance.

name: China CITIC Bank
desc: Chinese joint-stock commercial bank majority-owned by CITIC Group, providing corporate and retail banking, credit cards and wealth management.
markets: Customers across China, with international business through Hong Kong; no major overseas retail operations.
rationale: Chinese commercial bank with a domestic customer base; F1 hospitality could suit corporate clients, but fit is limited.

name: China Construction Bank
desc: One of China's four large state-owned banks, among the world's largest by assets, providing corporate, retail and international banking.
markets: Mainly China, with branches in Hong Kong, Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and elsewhere.
rationale: Very large Chinese bank with overseas branches; F1 could support corporate hospitality but overseas retail brand is small.

name: CIBC
desc: One of Canada's large banks, tracing its roots to 1867, providing personal and business banking, credit cards and wealth management.
markets: Serves customers in Canada and the US, including commercial and wealth clients.
rationale: North American bank; the Canadian Grand Prix offers hospitality for business clients, but footprint is limited to Canada and the US.

name: Citibanamex
desc: One of Mexico's largest banks, founded in 1884, offering retail banking, credit cards, SME and corporate banking, and wealth services.
markets: Customers across Mexico; ownership is being separated from Citi, with no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Large Mexican bank; the Mexico City Grand Prix offers strong home-market hospitality and brand exposure.
changed: Being separated from Citi, with a minority stake sold in 2025

name: Clifford Capital
desc: Singapore specialist finance company providing export credit, project finance and infrastructure and marine lending to companies, especially in Asia.
markets: Based in Singapore, financing companies mainly in Asia; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: B2B project and export lender with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality is possible through the Singapore Grand Prix.

name: CloudWalk
desc: Brazilian fintech running the InfinitePay payments business and the JIM.com platform, offering card machines, digital accounts, credit and merchant services.
markets: Serves Brazilian merchants and small businesses; no verified significant overseas operations.
rationale: Brazilian payments brand with strong marketing; payments rivals already sponsor F1, and the Sao Paulo Grand Prix fits.

name: CreditAccess Grameen
desc: Indian microfinance company providing small joint-liability loans to women in rural and semi-urban areas as a non-bank lender.
markets: Lends to rural customers across India; no international operations.
rationale: Microfinance lender serving rural borrowers, with no premium brand use for F1; very weak fit.

name: Deutsche Bank
desc: Germany's largest bank, founded in 1870, operating Corporate Bank, Investment Bank, Private Bank and DWS asset management businesses.
markets: Serves clients in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific with corporate, investment and private banking.
rationale: Global bank in a sector where rivals sponsor F1; German Grand Prix history and client hospitality suit it.

name: Doha Bank
desc: Qatari commercial bank founded in 1979, offering retail, corporate, private and Islamic-style banking, plus trade finance.
markets: Customers mainly in Qatar; the bank also has branches in a few other countries.
rationale: Qatari bank with domestic focus; the Qatar Grand Prix gives home-market hospitality for corporate clients.

name: Dubai Islamic Bank
desc: World's first full-service Islamic bank, founded in 1975, and the largest Islamic bank in the UAE, offering Sharia-compliant banking.
markets: Customers in the UAE, with subsidiaries abroad including Pakistan, offering Sharia-compliant retail, corporate and treasury services.
rationale: Gulf bank with a strong brand; the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix gives hospitality and regional reach.

name: Emirates NBD
desc: Middle East banking group formed in 2007 from Emirates Bank and National Bank of Dubai, offering retail and corporate banking.
markets: Operates in the UAE, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkey through DenizBank, India, Singapore and the UK.
rationale: Large regional bank with sports sponsorship appetite; the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix offers hospitality and brand reach.

name: Erste Group
desc: Austrian banking group serving about 16 million customers in Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, Romania, Hungary, Croatia and Serbia.
markets: Operates across Central and Eastern Europe under brands such as Erste Bank, Ceska sporitelna and Slovenska sporitelna.
rationale: Central European retail bank; the Austrian and Hungarian Grands Prix fit its markets, though reach is regional.

name: First Abu Dhabi Bank
desc: UAE's largest bank, formed in 2017 by merging National Bank of Abu Dhabi and First Gulf Bank, serving corporate clients.
markets: Operates in the UAE and other markets across the Middle East, Africa, Asia and Europe, plus North America.
rationale: Abu Dhabi bank with international corporate clients; the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix offers hospitality and brand reach.
